label: Ignatius of Antioch addresses the church at Magnesia on the Maeander

date.note: Ignatius wrote en route to martyrdom at Rome. Eusebius (Hist. eccl. 3.36) places the journey under Trajan (reigned 98–117), traditionally c. 107–110; the range brackets the later part of Trajan's reign. A minority redates the letters to c. 125–150 (Barnes 2008).

primary.cite: Ignatius, To the Magnesians, salutation; also 2 (their bishop Damas)

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, p. 186

notes: Magnesia ad Maeandrum/Leukophrys (Pleiades 599778), not Magnesia ad Sipylum (550706) nor the Thessalian Magnesia region (540923). The Apocalypse does not mention Magnesia, so this is Ignatius' independent attestation; Harnack p. 186 calls the church 'earlier than Trajan's reign, undoubtedly (see Ignatius).' Ignatius names Damas as their bishop.
